what_it_shows: Goo-net body-type guide: eight usual body types (sedan, coupe, open car/roadster, station wagon, one-box, minivan, SUV, hatchback/compact) plus kei-car class (660cc, 3.4m x 1.48m x 2m, 4 seats); site nav adds hybrid/EV, commercial, camping car, kei truck/van, bus/truck, welfare vehicle

Rose Bikes: Gravel, Rennrad, MTB, Urban and Trekking, E-Bike; sub-split by use (Adventure/Everyday/Race gravel; Race/Endurance road; XC/Trail/Downhill/Dirt MTB; Urban/Trekking) with e-versions cross-listed under E-Bike
AutoScout24: vehicle tabs Cars, Motorcycles, Caravans, Trucks, Trailers; car body-type quick links Compact, SUV and Pick-up, Transporter, Convertible, Van, Sedan, Station wagon, Coupe
UNECE page hosting Special Resolution No.1 (S.R.1) common definitions of vehicle categories, masses and dimensions

Google Vehicles & Parts: Vehicles = Aircraft, Motor Vehicles (cars/trucks/vans, golf carts, motorcycles and scooters, off-road ATVs/UTVs/go-karts, recreational vehicles, snowmobiles), Watercraft (motor boats, personal watercraft, sailboats, yachts); parts in a separate sibling branch

Wikipedia car body styles (sedan, hatchback, estate, coupe, convertible, roadster, targa, SUV, crossover, MPV, pickup, panel van, ute and others) with regional synonyms; states styles vary by use, market position, location and era

YachtWorld boat-type facet: Power vs Sail, then about 55 power classes (bowrider, center console, trawler, RIB, pontoon, PWC, tender...) and about 28 sail classes (sloop, ketch, catamaran, dinghy...); separate facets for drive type, make, length, price
EU Directive 2013/53/EU: craft 2.5-24 m; design categories A-D by wind force and wave height printed on builder plate; excludes canoes, kayaks, surfboards, racing boats, historic craft

Cycle Trader single Motorcycles-by-Category facet with about 30 values (cruiser, standard, touring, sportbike, custom, dirt bike, scooter, dual sport, trike, moped...) that also lists trailers, PWC, snowmobiles, utility carts and e-bikes in one list

Wikipedia: no universal system for classifying motorcycles; six commonly recognised categories (standard, cruiser, touring, sport, off-road, dual-purpose); scooters, mopeds, minibikes and trikes often excluded; legal and sport-body classes are separate

ISO 4210-2:2023 bicycle safety scope: young adult, city and trekking, mountain, racing (incl. folding) by saddle-height bands; excludes delivery bikes, recumbents, tandems, BMX and competition bikes; smaller ones fall under ISO 8098 or toy rules

FAA aircraft categories (airplane, glider, rotorcraft, lighter-than-air, powered lift, powered parachute, weight-shift control) with classes (SEL, SES, MEL, MES, helicopter, gyroplane, airship, balloon); type = make/model; separate certification categories (normal, utility, experimental, light sport...)
Trade-A-Plane top-level category Single Engine Piston; copy names Cessna, Mooney, Piper as leading makers and the Piper PA-28 Cherokee as a model line with many variants

Autohome vehicle levels: micro A00, small A0, compact A, mid B, upper-mid C, large D; SUVs and MPVs each in size grades; plus sports car, pickup, micro van, light bus, micro truck; defined by wheelbase, length and displacement
Car classification schemes: ISO 3833 terms; EC segments A-F, J, M, S; Euro NCAP, US EPA (volume), NHTSA (weight), IIHS, China GB/T 3730.1 (length or wheelbase); kei and microcar classes

RVIA RV types: travel trailer, fifth wheel, expandable, folding camping trailer, truck camper, sport utility RV, park model, motorhome Types A, B, C, with new-price ranges; excludes mobile homes, off-road vehicles, snowmobiles
UK vocabulary: campervan (converted van, pop-top or high-top) versus motorhome (purpose-built: low-profile, overcab/Luton, A-class); differs from US Class A/B/C

Baby transport: wheeled devices split into prams (lying, newborn) and strollers (sitting, forward); UK/US term differences (pram/baby carriage, pushchair/buggy/stroller); carrycot, travel system, twin, jogging; on-body carriers listed separately
E-bike legal classes: EU/UK EPAC (EN 15194; 250 W, 25 km/h, pedal-assist only) counted as a bicycle; speed pedelec L1e-B moped; US Class 1/2/3 by throttle and 20/28 mph; classes are measured specs

Antique, vintage and classic age bands disagree between clubs (AACA 25+ years, CCCA Full Classics 1915-1948, vintage 1919-1930), insurers and US states (Michigan 26 years, Colorado 32); era is a label not a type
Auto Care VCdb: normalized Year-Make-Model fitment database with 175k+ vehicle applications, 2.4M configurations and 16k off-highway units; parts catalogues key on make-model-year

eBay Motors Cars and Trucks: shop by body type (convertible, coupe, hatchback, minivan, sedan, SUV, truck, van, wagon), by vehicle type (classics, collector, exotics, electric and hybrid), by make and popular model; sibling nodes Boats, Motorcycles, Powersports, Other vehicles and trailers

mobile.de: tabs for cars, electric, motorcycles, e-bikes, motorhomes and caravans, vans, trucks; car types Kombi, Limousine, Cabrio/Roadster, SUV/Geländewagen, Sportwagen/Coupé, Van/Minibus, Kleinwagen with listing counts; use-case shortcuts such as family cars are views

Buychari bicycle types: sport cycles (road, MTB, cross-bike, gravel, cyclocross, e-bike), casual (mini-velo, folding, track/pist, BMX, fat bike), and 軽快車 city cycle (mamachari) and electric-assist; model names used as examples

Bicycle types listed by function, riders, gearing, sport, propulsion, rider position and frame; says the categories overlap; includes cargo, tandem, recumbent, unicycle, tricycle, velomobile and e-bike

Small boats guide: paddlecraft (kayaks sit-in/sit-on-top/fishing, canoes, rowboats, SUPs), inflatables (low/high pressure), dinghies (two senses), RIBs, PWCs, jon boats, trailerable sail and power boats; example makers and models named
470 dinghy is a World Sailing International one-design class (Olympic since 1976) built by licensed builders, so a class design is a named form not tied to one maker

Controller aircraft categories: jets, turboprops, piston, light sport, piston and turbine helicopters, amphibious/floatplanes, experimental/homebuilt; parts, avionics and hangar equipment are separate
Decathlon UK kayaks: Inflatable vs Rigid sub-categories (143 items), with sit-on-top, sit-inside, fishing, pedal-drive, touring and packraft models from Itiwit, Tahe, Sevylor, Aqua Marina and others

Polaris snowmobile types: trail, mountain, crossover, widetrack, sport-utility, entry-level, youth, defined by track and ski design; maker lines (RMK, Switchback, INDY, Voyageur, TITAN) with variants, engine options and 2026 MSRP from about 10,500 to 23,200 USD
Handcar/draisine/railbike: pump and push trolleys with many regional names, used for track maintenance, now tourism and vintage-railway racing; historic US makers Sheffield, Kalamazoo, Buda
Railtrader: commercial rail equipment (tank, hopper and box cars, maintenance-of-way machines, hi-rail trucks, push carts); shows rail vehicles are mostly a commercial market
EU vehicle categories: L (mopeds, motorcycles, quads, small 3-4 wheelers), M (passenger vehicles, essentially cars), N (goods vehicles), O (trailers and semitrailers)
UNECE consolidated resolution R.E.3: categories L1-L7, M1-M3, N1-N3, O1-O4, G off-road suffix, motor caravan as special-purpose M1, and M1 bodywork codes AA saloon to AF multi-purpose
Trailer category O defined by maximum mass: O1 to 750 kg, O2 to 3,500 kg, O3 to 10,000 kg, O4 above; includes drawbar and semi-trailers
Science Museum Group collection site: a Railways theme and separate National Railway Museum and Locomotion sites; shows museums treating rail as its own domain; no vehicle-type tree on the page
